info.title: KANE HACK OS API
info.description:
Every Hack OS operation: the Codex skills, `kanehack` CLI, MCP and the website all call these.

**139 operations**: 92 live in production, 23 new on this branch, 24 planned (return 501).

### TestMu AI access key
When `TESTMU_KEY_REQUIRED=true`, every non-public operation needs a TestMu AI access key:
- **Browser:** connect once at `/api/v1/auth/testmu/start`. TestMu AI redirects back with the key, we verify it and set the `hd_testmu` cookie (the key itself is never stored).
- **CLI / agents:** send `X-TestMu-Username` and `X-TestMu-Access-Key` (or `Authorization: Basic base64(username:access_key)`).

A pairing bearer token (`kanehack pair`) still says *who* you are; the TestMu key says the call is allowed at all. Send both headers if you use both.

### Envelope
Every JSON response uses the same envelope (`status`, `message`, `data`, `actions`, `error`, `fallback.text`…). Errors carry `error.code`, `next_action` and a `manual_route` web fallback.

```text
The photo pipeline posts each tagged event photo here once (multipart):
  file      the JPEG (the pipeline resizes to fit the 4.5 MB request limit)
  key       stable id for the photo (content hash); re-sending is a no-op
  teams     one or more team slugs the photo was matched to
  people    optional P-codes of people the pipeline face-matched (suggestions only)
  caption   optional, shown under the photo

suggested person and every current member of the team has said yes to
photo publication. Anything else is stored privately and HELD for review
in /ops/media ("held for review"), never published on a camera match alone.
```

post.summary: [new] save the profile and activate TestMu AI; returns the access key once.
post.description:
**Status:** NEW on testmu-api  
**Access:** No TestMu key (handshake, docs or server-to-server with its own secret).  
**Plan v2.5:** not in the plan (site-specific).  
**Source:** `src/app/api/v1/auth/register/route.ts`

```text
POST /api/v1/auth/register: save the profile and activate TestMu AI; returns the access key once.
No TestMu key needed: this is where it comes from.
  { name, email (the Luma one), linkedin, x, github?, password (8+), looking?: "yes",
    proof_password? | proof_code? (only when the email already has an account),
    testmu_password? (the TestMu AI password, when it differs from `password`) }
The same profile as /register. Saves it, then activates the person on TestMu AI
with it and their TestMu AI password: testmu_password, else password, else
proof_password. The password is passed on, never stored. TestMu answers with their
username + access key, returned here ONCE as data.testmu. Send them as
X-TestMu-Username / X-TestMu-Access-Key on every call after. The key isn't stored (only a fingerprint).
409 needs_proof: the email has an account; resend with proof_password or proof_code.
needs_action with data.testmu_error.reason "wrong_password": the email already has a
TestMu AI account with another password. Resend with proof_password + testmu_password.
```
